rationale: Round 0 built and passed, so the table is pushed moderately more aggressive while respecting this benchmark's sensitivity: stepanov_vector is a small, template-heavy, abstraction-focused benchmark with tight inner loops (sum, accumulate, heapsort) where runtime overhead compounds, so SUB (cheap, correct, high static-analysis friction) and FLA (strongest structural disguise for the 11KB main and control-dominated helpers) carry the highest weights, with SPLIT boosted to complement FLA by pre-splitting blocks so flattening has more dispatch structure to hide. BCF stays mid-range because its opaque predicates are the main size/runtime cost driver and the 17.7KB text budget is small. IBR and ICALL get moderate weights to obscure the call/branch graph — the templated heapsort instantiations give ICALL real diversity value — but their CorrectnessRisk weights are kept above SUB/FLA since vtable-style indirect references in C++ template code can interact badly. IGV is weighted lowest and risk-highest: the benchmark is constant/global-data heavy (constant folding, lookup tables), and indirecting globals is where correctness breaks show up for this profile.
